html:
Bolivia is a landlocked country in the Andes and the Amazon lowlands of South America, independent since 1825 and named after Simón Bolívar.

Its high plateau around Lake Titicaca was home to Tiwanaku and later part of the Inca Empire. Under Spain it was Upper Peru, and the silver mountain of Potosí made it one of the richest places in the Spanish empire. Independence was won in 1825 and Antonio José de Sucre became its first president. The capital is Sucre, but the government sits in La Paz.

Bolivia lost land in war after war:

  • The War of the Pacific of 1879 to 1884 cost it its coast to Chile.
  • Brazil took the rubber region of Acre in the early 1900s.
  • The Chaco War of 1932 to 1935 against Paraguay cost it most of the Chaco.

Tin replaced silver as the main export, and a few tin barons dominated the country. The National Revolution of 1952 nationalised the mines, broke up great estates and gave the vote to the Native majority. Coups and military rule followed; Che Guevara was killed in Bolivia in 1967 while trying to start a guerrilla war.

In 2006 Evo Morales, an Aymara coca grower, became the first Indigenous president. The constitution of 2009 renamed the country the Plurinational State of Bolivia.
sum: Bolivia is a landlocked country in the Andes and the Amazon lowlands of South America, independent since 1825 and named after Simón Bolívar.
